concepts.proposed_markdown:
## Native NetSuite integration boundary

Metronome's Public Beta NetSuite integration supports direct billing and revenue-system use cases. A contract selects a customer configuration: billing mode sends finalized invoices to NetSuite for NetSuite-owned distribution, tax, and collection, while revenue mode sends invoices after another system attempts payment and creates payment objects when successful. Product custom fields map Metronome line items to NetSuite item IDs, and zero-dollar prepaid-consumption invoices require a separate Commit Application item. Billing status and errors appear under `external_invoice`; revenue-system status and errors appear under `revenue_system_invoices`; invoice and payment sync webhooks expose outcome signals, and an item-mapping failure can be corrected before a manual UI resend. The guide does not turn those signals into guarantees of delivery, payment finality, tax correctness, revenue posting, settlement, or reconciliation. The beta excludes custom currencies and account hierarchy, assumes compatible standard NetSuite configuration, and assigns client-specific changes and sandbox validation to the client.
warnings: Keep billing-provider and revenue-system configuration, identifiers, status surfaces, and responsibilities distinct.
Do not extend Metronome status or webhook signals into NetSuite acceptance, payment finality, accounting, tax, settlement, or reconciliation guarantees.

concepts.proposed_markdown:
### Native NetSuite billing and revenue-system delivery

A contract can route a finalized invoice to NetSuite as billing provider, after which NetSuite owns distribution, tax calculation, and payment collection. Alternatively, NetSuite can be the revenue system while another provider bills: Metronome sends the invoice after a payment attempt, adds a linked payment object on success, can represent a first-attempt failure as `OPEN`, and can later update it to `PAID` after a successful reattempt. Billing-mode observations live under `external_invoice`, while revenue-mode observations live under `revenue_system_invoices`; failure information and sync notifications support diagnosis, and a corrected item mapping can be followed by a manual resend. These surfaces do not prove external acceptance, customer delivery, payment finality, tax correctness, revenue posting, settlement, or reconciliation.
warnings: Do not conflate Metronome invoice finalization with NetSuite distribution, collection, payment, tax, or accounting completion.
Treat the documented manual resend as scoped recovery guidance, not a general retry, exactly-once, or idempotency guarantee.

### NetSuite customer and contract routing layers

A Metronome customer can hold multiple NetSuite billing or revenue-system configurations, but a configuration does not route invoices until the relevant configuration ID is selected on a contract. Billing configuration sends finalized contract invoices to NetSuite for NetSuite-owned distribution, tax, and collection. Revenue-system configuration sends invoices and available payment state after billing occurs elsewhere; a failed first payment can leave the NetSuite invoice `OPEN`, followed by a retroactive `PAID` update after later success. The external `netsuite_customer_id`, account-level `delivery_method_id`, and contract selectors `billing_provider_configuration_id` or `revenue_system_configuration_id` remain distinct identity layers.
warnings: Do not treat customer-level configuration as invoice routing without the contract selection.
Do not conflate the external NetSuite customer ID, account delivery-method ID, customer configuration IDs, and contract selectors.
